page: Google Cloud Platform m3-ultramem-64 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. The processor is equipped with a 54 MB L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

The defining characteristic of this instance is its massive memory capacity, offering 1952.0 GB of RAM, which translates to 30.5 GB of memory per core. This high memory-to-vCPU ratio is designed for memory-bound workloads. The instance does not include local NVMe SSD storage or bundled GPUs, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes, and parallel processing tasks rely entirely on the CPU.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with a Passmark CPU score of 55325.27 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 16753.0. Database operations are a key strength, scoring in the top 25% on Passmark database tests with 26390.07 operations. Memory bandwidth is measured at 151.05 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 61.86 GB/sec for large-block write operations. The CPU also demonstrates strong performance in software compilation and ray tracing.

Given the massive RAM allocation, this instance represents a specialized hardware profile with high resource density. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require keeping massive datasets entirely in memory, avoiding the latency of disk I/O. The m3-ultramem-64 is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, real-time data analytics, and memory-intensive scientific computing.
